source: Brønsted acid–base systems in water at 25 °C. Acid constants Ka of acetic, formic and phosphoric acid and of the hydrogen sulfate ion: OpenStax Chemistry 2e (2019, CC BY 4.0), Appendix H 'Ionization Constants of Weak Acids'; the first ionization of sulfuric acid is complete (Ka1 more than 10², OpenStax Chemistry 2e §14.5 'Polyprotic Acids'); both pages copied in acid-base/. Thermodynamic pK of glycine at 25 °C by cells without liquid junction: E. J. King, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 73, 155 (1951), as transcribed in D. D. Perrin, Dissociation Constants of Organic Bases in Aqueous Solution (1965), entry perrin3140 of the IUPAC Digitized pKa Dataset v2.4 (doi:10.5281/zenodo.7236452, CC BY-NC 4.0, reproduced by permission of IUPAC); its glycine rows are copied in acid-base/. A system names a molecule of molecules.json; protonatedSites are atom indices of its catalogue structure that carry an extra proton in the most protonated form, and each step takes the proton off its site
